task_retrieval_key:
A two-year-old boy was referred to our department due to a distal diaphyseal fracture of the left femur. He is the first child of non-consanguineous parents. At birth, his weight, length, and occipital-frontal circumference were around the 25th percentile. His mother, a 26-year-old primagravida, had no history of spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, or neonatal mortalities and was married to a 27-year-old unrelated man. At birth, the child had plagiocephaly and was treated with a cranial band (Care band), which he wore for 23 hours per day until he was one year old. No skull radiographs were taken at that time. His development included motor delay, but other developmental skills were within the normal range. There was no history of visual, auditory, or other neurological symptoms, nor was there any history of anorexia, weight loss, or muscular hypotonia. Examination at the age of two years showed a pleasant boy with mild and unnoticeable facial features, including frontal bossing and slight facial asymmetry with incomplete auricular folding. There were no signs of leontiasis ossea, Cushingoid facies, macrocephaly, retarded growth, or muscular hypotonia. Neurological, ophthalmological, and auditory evaluations were normal, with no history of seizures or non-motor developmental delay. Audiometric evaluation ruled out peripheral hearing loss. Ophthalmological examination showed normal vision with no strabismus or other eye issues. Musculo-skeletal examination revealed relative ligamentous hyperlaxity with patellar instability and thoraco-lumbar scoliosis of 32 degrees.
